tagline: Out of Bliss, past springs running out of the canyon wall.
intro: US 30 leaves the interstate at Bliss and dips into the Hagerman Valley and a canyon of the Snake River, then runs southeast through Hagerman, Buhl and Filer toward Twin Falls. Along the east wall of the canyon, streams and rivulets come straight out of the rock, many of them plain to see from the road with the river in front.

They are outlets of the Snake River Aquifer, which moves through porous volcanic rock and is believed to be fed by the Big Lost River, a river that disappears into the lava near Arco, about 90 miles away.

moments.title: Thousand Springs State Park
moments.text: In the Box Canyon unit, between walls 250 feet high, the eleventh-largest spring in North America gushes 180,000 gallons a minute.

moments.title: Hagerman Fossil Beds National Monument
moments.text: The Hagerman Horse Quarry has given up 20 complete skeletons of a zebra-like ancestor of today's horse, the best known of more than 180 species found in these beds.

moments.title: Buhl
moments.text: The Trout Capital of the World, by its own account, ringed with hatcheries that raise most of the rainbow trout eaten in the United States.
